transcript.text:
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's workout meeting for the Harbor Point Properties restructuring proposal. As you all know, we have an $8 million term loan secured by the borrower's office building, equipment, and receivables. Harbor Point has requested a 12-month maturity extension, a waiver of the current financial covenant, and release of $900,000 of equipment collateral due to weaker-than-expected occupancy reducing their debt-service coverage.

Before I can record the final terms, I need each of you -- risk, relationship coverage, legal, and collateral management -- to provide your findings update and identify the supporting document or policy for any recommendations you have. I'll be including the relevant sources in the meeting minutes. Let's go ahead and get started.

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from the covenant testing file I reviewed this week. Harbor Point's leverage is currently 0.3x above the permitted level. Under our workout policy, a covenant waiver is only allowed with a 9-month extension — not the 12 months the borrower requested — and requires a monthly leverage certificate. I should also note that I have not yet attached the testing file to the committee package, so I want to make sure everyone is aware of these findings now.

transcript.text: I have an important update from the relationship side. This morning I received a signed term sheet from Harbor Point committing the owners to inject exactly $1,200,000 of new equity at restructuring closing. This commitment has not yet been entered in the relationship system, so I want to make sure it's on the record now. The signed term sheet is my supporting document.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a critical legal finding to share. While reviewing the intercreditor agreement this week, I confirmed that the senior lender must give written consent before any equipment collateral is released. That consent has not yet been requested. This directly impacts the borrower's request to release $900,000 of equipment collateral — we cannot proceed with that release until the senior lender's written consent is obtained. The intercreditor agreement is my supporting document.

transcript.text: I have a collateral management finding to share. Yesterday I completed a collateral review showing that receivables are the weakest and most volatile part of the collateral package. Under our collateral policy, this requires a weekly borrowing-base certificate throughout the extension period. I should also note that I have not yet updated the monitoring schedule to reflect this requirement. The collateral review I completed yesterday is my supporting document, along with the collateral policy.
